name: The Hyundai Seoul
summary: Seoul's largest department store: sunlit glass-roofed atriums, an indoor garden, a 12 m waterfall and nonstop pop-ups in Yeouido.
description: Opened in 2021 in the Parc.1 complex, The Hyundai Seoul gives almost half its floor area to open space, gardens and a glass roof that floods the atriums with daylight. Luxury and contemporary labels share the floors with a rotating programme of brand pop-ups and art exhibitions that draw young Seoul on weekends. The basement food hall is one of the city's biggest, and the 5th-floor Sounds Forest indoor garden is the place to sit down. It is the most 'future Seoul' of the city's department stores and an easy half-day with parents.
highlights: Sounds Forest indoor garden under the glass roof (5F)
12-metre indoor waterfall and daylight-filled atrium
Rotating brand pop-ups and exhibitions (B1–B2 and event halls)
Huge basement food hall and dessert counters
tips: CLOSED Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep for Chuseok (Hyundai Department Store notice); go Sat 26 onwards.
From home, Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal then Line 9 express to Yeouido is the fastest subway route; the store connects underground from Yeouido Station.
Weekend afternoons are packed with pop-up queues — arrive at 10:30 opening or on a weekday.
Foreign shoppers can claim tax refunds; bring passports for all five.

name: Shinsegae Department Store Gangnam
summary: Korea's top-grossing department store, right above Express Bus Terminal: Sweet Park dessert hall, House of Shinsegae dining, luxury floors.
description: Shinsegae Gangnam sits on top of Express Bus Terminal station, one stop from home on Line 3, and is the store Seoulites treat as the benchmark. Its renovated food floors are the draw: Sweet Park (opened Feb 2024) packs 43 dessert brands into about 5,300 m² of Grand Central-style arcades, House of Shinsegae (June 2024) is a dim, hotel-like dining and wine hall open until 22:00, and Shinsegae Market sells premium produce and gifts. Above them are every major luxury house, Korean designers and a big beauty floor. Easy to pop into repeatedly during the week.
highlights: Sweet Park — Korea's largest dessert hall (43 brands incl. Pierre Marcolini, Mille & Un, Fortnum & Mason)
House of Shinsegae — low-lit restaurant hall and ~5,000-bottle Wine Cellar, open to 22:00
Shinsegae Market premium grocery and Chuseok gift sets
Full luxury and K-beauty floors under one roof
tips: NEAR HOME: one stop on Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal (or a short taxi); combine with Goto Mall underneath.
CLOSED Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep; open Sat 26 onward (extended hours to 20:30 Fri–Sun).
House of Shinsegae restaurants stay open to 22:00 (last order 1 h before) — good for a late family dinner after the store closes.
Spend ₩50,000+ for 1 h free parking; foreign shoppers get tax refunds on eligible purchases (bring passports).

name: Shinsegae Department Store Main Store & The Heritage
summary: Korea's first department store (1930s building) plus The Heritage, a restored 1935 bank with Korean craft floor and a giant media facade.
description: Shinsegae's flagship faces the Bank of Korea roundabout between Myeongdong and Namdaemun Market: an early-20th-century main building joined to a modern wing. Across the lane, The Heritage (opened 9 April 2025) restores a 1935 bank — Seoul cultural heritage — with a Peter Marino-designed Chanel on 1–2F, a 4F museum of Myeongdong's retail history and House of Shinsegae Heritage on 5F showcasing Korean crafts with a dessert salon. After dark the store's wraparound digital media facade lights the whole square. The basement food hall is a long-time office-lunch favourite.
highlights: The Heritage: restored 1935 bank, 5F House of Shinsegae Heritage Korean craft gallery-shop and dessert salon
Shinsegae Square media facade on the main building after dark
4F museum on Myeongdong's retail history with restored 1930s–50s images
Basement food hall (11:00–21:30)

Line 4 Hoehyeon Station Exit 7 leads straight in; pair with Namdaemun Market (next door) or Myeongdong (5 min walk) — but Namdaemun is shut 24–27 Sep.
Come just after sunset to see the media facade, then eat in the food hall.

name: CHZZK LoL Park
summary: Riot's League of Legends home arena in Jongno, with a 101-seat PC room and LCK exhibits. No LCK matches during your trip.
description: LoL Park is Riot Games' purpose-built esports venue on the 3rd floor of the Gran Seoul tower in Jongno, home of the LCK (League of Legends Champions Korea) since 2018; Naver renamed it CHZZK LoL Park in December 2025. It holds a 450-seat arena, the 101-seat Riot PC room, the Bilgewater-themed café, a Riot Store, and a display of team uniforms and LCK history. Honest timing warning: the 2026 LCK season ended with the finals at KSPO Dome on 12–13 Sep, and Worlds 2026 runs in the USA from 15 Oct, so no LCK matches are scheduled here on 23–30 Sep. Off-season, it is a short pilgrimage: take photos, browse the merch, and play a few rounds in the PC room.
highlights: 450-seat LCK arena (open to view only on match days)
Riot PC room with 101 seats, run as a members-only PC room
Championship trophy photo zone in the Bilgewater Café (added April 2026)
Riot Store merchandise and displays of LCK team uniforms
tips: No LCK matches 23–30 Sep 2026: the season ended with the 13 Sep final and Worlds is in the USA from 15 Oct. Only go if someone is a League fan.
The PC room is members-only. Bring a Korean phone number or ask staff to help you sign up. Machines have an English client, but the ordering menus are mostly in Korean.
Take Exit 1 at Jonggak Station, about a 3-minute walk. It pairs easily with Insadong, Cheonggyecheon or Gwanghwamun on the same afternoon.
On match days the venue closes when the last match ends. Off-season hours are listed as 11:00–20:00, so call ahead.

name: T1 Base Camp Hongdae
summary: Faker's team's 24-hour PC café and fan museum, with pro-spec rigs, console party rooms and a T1 merch shop by Hongik Univ.
description: T1, the esports club of League of Legends legend Faker, runs this basement gaming café under the Megabox building near Hongik University Station. A stairway lit with LED tells the team history on the way down to a clean, bright PC room with Secretlab chairs and SteelSeries gear, a wall of signed jerseys, a life-size Faker figure, private console rooms, and a shop selling uniforms and peripherals. The PC zone runs 24 hours, and you can order Korean PC-bang snacks to your seat. It is the most polished way to try a Korean PC bang, even for people who are not T1 fans.
highlights: Pro-level gaming PCs set up the way the players have theirs
Life-size Faker figure, wall of signed jerseys and a T1-framed photo booth
Private console party rooms, good for a group of 5
Official T1 shop for jerseys, peripherals and phone cases
tips: The PC interface and food ordering are mostly in Korean. Keep Papago open, or ask staff to set up a non-member session.
Book a console room so all five of you can play together. Regular PC seats are in rows.
A bigger 476-pyeong Gangnam branch near Sinnonhyeon soft-opens on 3 Oct 2026, after your trip. Hongdae is the one open now.
Members pay less per hour than non-members. For a one-off visit, a 1–3 hour block is enough.

name: Readygo Active Game Park Gangnam
summary: Neon LED-floor game rooms by Sinnonhyeon: step on blue tiles, dodge red ones, 15 sweaty team minutes for ₩7,000 each.
description: This purple-neon playground opened on the 4th floor of a side-street building behind CGV Gangnam in late 2025. It is the Korean version of the "active gaming" craze. Each private room has an LED floor and wall that light up in patterns: the team hits blue tiles and avoids red ones as the levels speed up to 30, with a scoreboard and countdown on the wall. You pick a room by group size and a mode (team, battle, double battle or kids) and difficulty, and play one intense 15-minute session. A time-lapse video QR code comes on your receipt. Infinity-mirror corridors, an LED pixel-art wall, a drink bar with slushies and a props-and-hairdryer corner make it feel like a futuristic arcade rather than a gym.
highlights: Private LED floor-and-wall rooms. The mid-size room fits 2–6, so all five of you can play one team game.
Free time-lapse video of your run, delivered by QR code on the receipt
Infinity-mirror corridors and a touch LED wall for pixel-art photos
Slushie drink zone and props/hairdryer station for after the game
tips: Hidden gem: Kakao Map has more than 100 Naver blog write-ups, almost all from Korean families and friend groups, and it is barely known to foreign visitors.
Socks are compulsory with the indoor shoes provided (they sell socks if you forget). Wear something with pockets for the locker key, and tie long hair back.
Book a mid-size room (2–6 people) via Naver Booking or by phone. There is a ₩5,000 room deposit, then ₩7,000 per adult. Arrive 10 minutes before your slot.
Start on Easy. Korean reviewers say even Easy leaves you drenched in 15 minutes, so parents can join one game and then watch from the lounge.

reviews.text: Even easy mode is a real workout. After just 15 minutes you are covered in sweat, which makes it great cardio. You also get a free slushie for leaving a receipt review.

name: Golfzon Park Yeoksam Gangnam (2ON)
summary: Screen golf done properly: ten private bays with Golfzon's newest TwoVision NX Plus and 4K projectors, near Gangnam Station.
description: Screen golf is how Seoul actually plays golf. This Golfzon Park in a basement off Teheran-ro was upgraded in 2026 to TwoVision NX Plus, Golfzon's top simulator, on all ten bays, with 4K cinema projectors, moving swing plates and floor screens. It is one of the best-rated screen-golf venues in Gangnam on the Korean booking app Kimcaddie. Each bay is a private room with a sofa, so the family can play real Korean and overseas courses while ordering fried chicken and beer to the room. Rental clubs (recent Callaway, Ping and Cobra drivers), gloves, shoes and even T-shirts mean you can show up empty-handed.
highlights: Golfzon TwoVision NX Plus on all 10 bays, with a 4K projector and floor screen
Private bays with sofas. Food, beer and snacks are delivered to your room.
Well-kept rental clubs, shoes, gloves and T-shirts, plus a self-serve coffee corner
Runs 24 hours: staffed by day, self-service from 23:00 to 09:00
tips: Hidden gem for visitors: it has 9.9/10 from 1,167 reviews on Kimcaddie, but it is almost entirely Korean office workers and hardly any tourists.
When you book for five, ask whether they recommend one bay or two neighbouring bays, since five players in one bay makes 18 holes slow. First-timers should pick the 9-hole or 'easy' setting.
Come during staffed daytime hours so someone can set up the English menu. After 23:00 it runs unmanned and needs a Golfzon app booking.
Kakao Map lists it as open year-round (연중무휴). Chuseok week is a quiet time to get a bay.

reviews.text: A regular was delighted that NX Plus finally reached Yeoksam. It feels much more like a real course than the old NX, and the 24-hour opening is a big plus.

name: Spa Lei (women only)
summary: Women-only 24h bathhouse by Sinsa Station: seawater and open-air baths, a pine-fired bulhanjeungmak and famous body scrubs.
description: Spa Lei is a women-only sauna and jjimjilbang in Jamwon-dong, a few minutes' walk from Sinsa Station and one stop from home on Line 3. The spa styles itself on Eastern European bathhouses, with dark wood, framed photographs and a small open-air bath on a terrace, alongside a West Coast seawater bath, green-tea bath and a cold plunge that regulars rave about. The traditional bulhanjeungmak (fire-heated dome sauna) is lit with Gangwon pine at 5 am and opens at 10 am; there are also red-clay, charcoal and salt rooms. Seshin (Korean body scrub), oil massage, facials and nails are sold in-house, which is what most foreign reviewers come for.
highlights: Seshin body scrub, with oil or aroma add-ons
Pine-fired bulhanjeungmak dome sauna (opens 10:00)
Small open-air bath and terrace
Seawater bath and ice-cold plunge
tips: Women only: the men in the family need somewhere else, such as the JW Marriott Seoul sauna nearby at Express Bus Terminal.
Entry is ₩22,000 for 8 hours, then ₩2,000 an hour. Several September 2026 Naver reviewers were surprised by the overtime charge, so note your entry time.
Spa Lei went viral on Instagram in September 2026 and Naver reviewers report packed weekends and Chuseok-season crowds. Go on a weekday morning, or just after 10:00 when the fire sauna opens.
Book scrubs and massages at the desk as soon as you arrive, because slots fill on busy days. Staff speak some English, according to TripAdvisor reviewers.

name: SPAREX Dongmyo
summary: A modern 24h jjimjilbang on the 13th floor above Dongmyo Station, with a fire-kiln sauna, hinoki bath and city views, for ₩14,000.
description: SPAREX Dongmyo is a newer branch of the SPAREX chain, opened around 2024 on the 13th floor of the building beside Dongmyo Station. It replaces the big old-school bathhouses that closed after COVID, including Dragon Hill Spa and Siloam Sauna. It is bright and modern, with gender-separated baths and dry and wet saunas, then a shared hall in spa clothes with a bulhanjeungmak (fire-heated dome), hwangto clay, salt, ice and hinoki rooms. There is also a food court serving sikhye, roasted eggs and Korean set meals, a well-equipped gym and screen golf. Locals love it: 7,700+ Naver reviews single out how clean it is, its size and its fair price.
highlights: Bulhanjeungmak fire domes and a hinoki forest-bath room
13th-floor lounges with city views
Food court: sikhye, roasted eggs, jeyuk and miyeok-guk
Seshin body scrub packages
tips: Hidden gem: over 7,700 Naver visitor reviews but only a handful on TripAdvisor. Go straight out of Dongmyo Station Exit 6 and up to the 13th floor.
Entry is ₩14,000 from 05:00–20:00 or ₩16,000 from 20:00–05:00, valid for 24 hours. Parking is free for 3 hours (official Instagram, June 2026).
Bring your own shampoo and a few ₩1,000 notes or coins, because hairdryers are coin-operated. Baths close for cleaning late at night (women's roughly 23:00–01:00, men's 00:00–02:00).
Pair it with the Dongmyo flea market or Dongdaemun (one stop on Line 1 or 6). It is also a cheap, rainy-evening reset for a group of 5.

reviews.text: A September 2026 reviewer found everything clean because it is fairly new. They liked the high-floor views, the jeyuk and seaweed-soup dinner and the reasonable price, and plan to return.
Another reviewer found the scrub short and the food-court tteokbokki and ramyeon undercooked. They called the food the weak spot.
A traveller said their scrub was excellent and very thorough, and that they 'felt like a new woman'.

name: Han River Night Picnic, Games & Starlight Cruise
summary: Guided evening in Yeouido: chimaek picnic by the river, dalgona and ttakji games, then a 50-minute Han River cruise.
description: This small-group evening tour recreates the classic Seoul night out by the Han River. An English-speaking guide sets up chairs, tables and lamps in Yeouido Hangang Park for a chicken-and-beer (chimaek) picnic with soju and snacks, teaches traditional games like dalgona and ttakji, then boards a round-trip cruise from Yanghwa pier past lit bridges and the National Assembly. It removes all the logistics of doing it yourself and is a relaxed way for a mixed-age family to see the river at night.
